tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-10-23 against 5 independent sources. Removed unsupported claims (specific sponge colours, 12-21 m colour band, mineral-rich substrate, southern stingrays, turtles). Species now limited to those named at this site: grunts and parrotfish (PADI), frogfish and squid (Moorings). Depth 50 m is NOT confirmed: two sources list an implausible 1,500 ft and others give none; kept as curated estimate. Difficulty sources conflict (stlucia.org: mild drift, all levels; Moorings: intermediate to advanced; PADI: moderate current) - kept Advanced. Name origin: Moorings and Stolen Time both attribute it to Superman II filming at Petit Piton.

Re-audited 2026-10-23 with 4 independent sources plus the operator's own resort page. Depth: plateau 5-25 ft dropping to ~140 ft (scubastlucia.com); 15-60 ft (stlucia.org); 20-140 ft (ansechastanet.com). Species restricted to those named at this site. Note ansechastanet.com and scubastlucia.com belong to the same operator.

Re-audited 2026-10-23. 3 domains describe the Anse Cochon reef, but no source uses the exact label 'Pinnacles (Anse Cochon)': scubastlucia.com lists 'Anse Couchon' (steep boulder slope; seahorses, scorpionfish, cleaner shrimp); stlucia.org lists Anse Cochon South (reef, boulders, walls, pinnacles, max ~40 ft) and North (5-60 ft); bluewaterdivetravel.com lists Anse Cochon North/South reefs, beginner-friendly. Identity of this curated label is therefore approximate - flagged for review. Removed carried-forward hawksbill/flounder claims and unsupported organ-pipe coral/trench topography. Stored depth 18 m is unconfirmed (stlucia.org gives ~12 m for South).

Re-audited 2026-10-23 against 5 sources. Species: trumpetfish, filefish, seahorses (scubastlucia.com 'Pinnacles', stolentime.com, PADI); grouper (PADI, stlucia.org, stolentime.com); frogfish (PADI); jacks, snappers, morays (stlucia.org / stolentime.com). Unconfirmed whale shark/sunfish claims (Moorings, Stolen Time mention whale sharks passing in general) not included. Removed 'voted one of the 10 Best Dive Sites' (divein.com, not re-fetchable). Difficulty: Bluewater describes it as challenging/for experienced divers - kept Intermediate.

Re-audited 2026-10-23, exactly 3 detailed sources (ansechastanet.com only lists it as a boat dive, and is the same operator as scubastlucia.com so not counted). Turtles: scubastlucia.com and stlucia.org name hawksbill and green turtles; stolentime.com says turtles visit only occasionally - conflict noted. Removed carried-forward parrotfish, blue chromis, damselfish, moray eels, spiny lobster (no source today). Depth 12 m reflects plateau only; reef drops to 150 ft+.

Wreck deep-research 2026-10-23. islanderkeys.com now returns 'Account Suspended' and was dropped. No Wikipedia article exists for this wreck (searched). Conflicts flagged: sinking year 1986 (scubastlucia.com, PADI, caribbean-diving.com, stlucia.org, stolentime.com [October 1986], dune-world.com) vs 1985 (deeperblue.com, scubadiving.com); length 165 ft (most), 167 ft (stlucia.org lists both), 50-51 m; depth range 12-22 m depending on source. Tonnage, build year, original vessel name/history: NOT reported in any source - omitted. Sinking cause: deliberate scuttling as artificial reef by the Department of Fisheries (stolentime.com, caribbean-diving.com). Removed unsupported rudder/propeller intact, tuna/pelagics, red snapper; kept Pappy Mac story removed.

Re-audited 2026-10-23. ONLY 2 independent domains found (scubastlucia.com: boat dive at base of Gros Piton, creole wrasse/bar jack/southern sennet, corals and sponges; scubaverse.com: mix of wall and reef between the Pitons). ansechastanet.com lists it as a boat dive but is the same operator as scubastlucia.com. Below the 3-source threshold; validated left as-is, flagged. Entry type changed from shore to boat (scubastlucia.com lists Jalousie among boat dives). No source gives depth or difficulty - stored 15 m / Beginner unconfirmed. Removed carried-forward seahorses and trumpetfish.

Re-audited 2026-10-23 against 4 sources. Depth corrected from 40 m to 34 m (wall 60-110 ft per PADI and stlucia.org). Advanced per PADI (AOW + drift experience). Rays: PADI, stlucia.org; turtles/jacks/Bermuda chub/spotted drums/fire coral: stolentime.com (only that source). divein.com and tikaye.com could not be re-confirmed (403/no content) and were dropped.

Wreck deep-research 2026-10-23. No Wikipedia article exists (searched). divefairhelen.com and divingaway.com returned 503 on fetch and were dropped; claims previously sourced only to them (tonnage, September 1996, Dept of Fisheries, barracuda accompanying tow, 'interior deliberately left intact', 'effectively a wall dive') removed. Conflicts flagged: length 244 ft/75 m (scubaweather, stlucia.org, search snippets) vs 224 ft (one snippet) vs DeeperBlue's mention of ~350 ft dredgers (sister ship near Vieux Fort); depth 30 m (scubaverse), 33 m/108 ft (stlucia.org), 100 ft/30 m max with hull at 55 ft (deeperblue), ~34 m (snippet); orientation on its side (stlucia.org) vs upside-down from air pocket (deeperblue). Build year and tonnage: not reported by any source. Government purchase early 1990s: scubaweather only. Stored coordinates (14.05, -61.01) lie well north of Anse Cochon (~13.91, -61.06), where sources locate the wreck - flagged for coordinate review, not changed.

Re-audited 2026-10-23 against 5 sources. Corrected: entry changed shore->boat (scubastlucia.com lists it among boat dives; the 'shore entry', '20 minutes by boat from Anse Chastanet' and 'used for entry-level training' claims had no support); depth 14 m -> 27 m (stlucia.org 15-90 ft; stolentime.com says slope continues hundreds of feet); difficulty Beginner -> Intermediate because sources conflict (Bluewater: for more experienced divers; scubaverse: beginner-friendly; stolentime: watch depth). Removed 'healthiest coral on west coast', Gros Piton height, drift sections, generic 'tropical fish of many varieties'. Species from scubastlucia.com and stolentime.com only (sargassum triggerfish, barracuda).

Re-audited 2026-10-23. No source (scubastlucia.com, PADI, stlucia.org, moorings.com, scubaverse.com, stolentime.com, bluewaterdivetravel.com) lists a site named 'The Drift (Pitons)'. The drift character of the Piton coast is documented only under Superman's Flight and Fairyland. Previous validated=true is not supported and has been set to false; recommend merging with or removing in favour of Superman's Flight. Species claims (turtles, stingrays, eagle rays) removed - not site-specific.

Re-audited 2026-10-23 against 4 sources. Name translation conflict: scubastlucia.com says Patois 'Large Reef'; stolentime.com says 'Great House'; moorings.com lists the alias 'The Big House'. Depth not firmly sourced (stlucia.org: starts ~40 ft, wall lip ~50 ft); stored 30 m unconfirmed. Marine life: only occasional large barracuda (stolentime.com) is site-specific; other species lists dropped.

tags.name: El Pirata Shipwreck
tags.qa_notes: Re-searched 2026-10-23 (wreck deep-research). No dive operator, DeeperBlue, PADI, or maritime source names a wreck called 'El Pirata' at Vieux Fort; DeeperBlue lists other wrecks (Wawinet 'Atlantic', Dredger, SK2, a WWII plane wreck at Vieux Fort) but not this one. OSM tags remain the only evidence (non-dangerous wreck visible at high and low tide). Vessel name, build date, length, tonnage, sinking cause: none found in 2+ sources. Remains unvalidated.

tags.name: Fairyland
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-10-23 against 5+ sources. site_type reef->wall (scubastlucia.com 'one of the most colorful walls'; PADI and Bluewater 'reef wall'); depth 15->18 m (plateau 40-60 ft per scubastlucia.com/stolentime.com; stlucia.org lists 40-200 ft). Corrected attribution: lobsters/stingrays/flounders/octopuses come from moorings.com, not scubastlucia.com. Creole wrasse and chromis re-confirmed by stolentime.com.

tags.name: Maria Island Reef
tags.qa_notes: Re-searched 2026-10-23. stlucia.org (offshore small islands) says independent visits to the Maria Islands are not permitted and access is through organised tours; AFAR reports seasonal closure for bird nesting and snorkelling as the main reef activity. No dive operator lists a scuba site at Maria Island. Remains unvalidated.
